Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

The game works, and now we want prizes.

The quiz settings get a new field, "Number of winners" (a number, at least 1, 3 by default).

Scoring:

- Each correct answer gives one point.
- Players with equal points are ranked by speed: the total time of their correct answers wins when it is lower. The time of an answer runs from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick.
- Players don't see points during the game.

Speed now decides ties, so all players must get each question at the same moment: the big screen and the phones must follow the moderator close to instantly.

After "End quiz":

- The big screen shows the leaderboard: one list item for each player, in order, with the place, the name, and the points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points").
- Each player's phone shows the place ("Place 2 of 5") and the points ("3 points").

Picking the winners (N is the number of winners):

- The "Top N" button (for example, "Top 3") makes the first N players of the leaderboard the winners.
- The "Draw" button is for ties. Every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed doesn't matter here). Each click draws again.
- Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
- The "Reset winners" button removes the winners.
- Winners get the "Winner" mark on the leaderboard, and their phones show "You won!". Both update live.

## Stack & Serving
- Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4.1, SQLite3 (all database files stored under `storage/`).
- Propshaft + Importmap + Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus); no Node.js build step.
- `bin/serve` prepares the SQLite database (`db:prepare`), compiles assets (`assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in production mode on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` over plain HTTP (no SSL redirect, accepts all host names).

## Moderator Area (`/moderate`)
- Protected by HTTP Basic authentication in `Moderate::BaseController` using constant-time `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare` against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- Models:
  - `Quiz` (`title` required) has many `questions` ordered by `position, id`.
  - `Question` (`body` required, `position`, `active` default `true`) has many `options` ordered by `position, id`.
  - `Option` (`body` required, `correct` default `false`, `position`).
- Question option validation runs on submitted form rows (`Question#option_rows`) inside a transaction:
  - Blank option rows are skipped.
  - Requires at least 2 non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`) and at least 1 correct option (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`).
  - On validation failure, no DB writes occur and all submitted rows (including blanks, newly added rows, and checkboxes) are preserved in the re-rendered form.
- Dynamic option rows are handled by `app/javascript/controllers/option_rows_controller.js`.
- Active toggle on the quiz page submits immediately via `this.form.requestSubmit()`.

## Preview Mode (`/moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/preview`)
- Plays active questions in order (`quiz.active_questions`).
- Preview state (`step`, `score`, `picked_id`, `finished`) is passed via a signed token (`Rails.application.message_verifier(:quizzy_preview)`) in query/form parameters so no preview answers are stored in the database or session.

## Quiz Export & Import
- **Export** (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export`, linked as `"Export"` on the quiz page):
  - `Quiz#export_payload` builds `{ title, questions: [{ text, active, options: [{ text, correct }] }] }` ordered by `position, id` with no extra keys.
  - Rendered via `JSON.pretty_generate` inside a single `<pre class="code-block">` element.
- **Import** (`GET/POST /moderate/quizzes/import`, opened via `"Import quiz"` button on `/moderate`):
  - `QuizImport` validates JSON syntax, structure, non-blank title/question/option texts, boolean types for optional `active` (defaults to `true`) and `correct` (defaults to `false`), at least 2 options per question, and at least 1 correct option per question.
  - All database writes run inside `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction`, ensuring invalid payloads create nothing (neither quiz nor partial questions).
  - Successful import always creates a new `Quiz` (even if a quiz with the same title exists) and redirects to its moderator page.

## Live Game (Release 2)
- **Models**:
  - `Game` (`quiz_id`, unique 5-char `code`, `quiz_title` snapshot, `status`: `lobby | question_open | question_closed | finished`, `current_question_index`, monotonically increasing `version`).
  - `GameQuestion` & `GameOption`: snapshots of the quiz's active questions and their options created when starting a game (`Game.create_from_quiz!`), so inactive questions are skipped and later edits/deletes on the quiz never affect running or past games.
  - `Player` (`game_id`, `name`, unique `token`): stored in an HTTP-only signed cookie scoped per game (`cookies.signed["quizzy_player_#{game.id}"]`) so the same browser remembers the player within a game while remaining completely independent across multiple games of the same quiz.
  - `Answer` (`game_id`, `player_id`, `game_question_id`, `game_option_id`): unique index on `[player_id, game_question_id]` ensures changing an answer updates the single row in place (`last pick counts`).
- **Moderator Big Screen (`/moderate/games/:id`)**:
  - Protected by `Moderate::BaseController` HTTP Basic Auth; uses full-bleed `layouts/screen.html.erb`.
  - Lobby displays quiz title, plain-text join URL, inline SVG QR code (`rqrcode`), live `"Players: N"` counter, and `"Start"` button.
  - Open question shows `"Question X of Y"`, options, live `"Answers: A / P"` counter, and `"Finish"` button.
  - Closed question shows per-option counts, `"Correct"` badges on correct options, and `"Next"` (or `"End quiz"` on the last question).
  - Finished state shows `"The quiz is over"`.
- **Player Experience (`/play/:code`)**:
  - Public routes under `PlayController` (no moderator auth).

  - While `question_open`, player templates and broadcasts never reference `option.correct?` so correctness cannot leak in page source or WebSocket payloads.

class Game < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed finished].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K L M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :quiz_title, presence: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  def self.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    transaction do
      game = create!(
        quiz: quiz,
        quiz_title: quiz.title,
        code: generate_unique_code,
        status: "lobby",
        current_question_index: 0,
        version: 1
      )

      quiz.active_questions.includes(:options).order(:position, :id).each_with_index do |question, q_idx|
        gq = game.game_questions.create!(
          body: question.body,

class Game < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed finished].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K L M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :quiz_title, presence: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  def self.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    transaction do
      game = create!(
        quiz: quiz,
        quiz_title: quiz.title,
        code: generate_unique_code,
        status: "lobby",
        current_question_index: 0,
        version: 1
      )

      quiz.active_questions.includes(:options).order(:position, :id).each_with_index do |question, q_idx|
        gq = game.game_questions.create!(
          body: question.body,
          position: q_idx + 1
        )

        question.options.sort_by { |o| [ o.position, o.id ] }.each_with_index do |option, o_idx|
          gq.game_options.create!(
            body: option.body,
            correct: option.correct?,
            position: o_idx + 1
          )
        end
      end

      game
    end
  end

  def self.generate_unique_code
    loop do
      code = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET.sample }.join
      return code unless exists?(code: code)
    end
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question_open?
    status == "question_open"
  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"
  end

  def finished?
    status == "finished"
  end

  def ordered_questions
    game_questions.includes(:game_options).order(:position, :id).to_a
  end

  def total_questions
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_question
    return nil if lobby? || finished?

    ordered_questions[current_question_index]
  end

  def last_question?
    total = total_questions
    total.zero? || current_question_index >= total - 1
  end

  def players_count
    players.count
  end

  def current_answers_count
    question = current_question
    return 0 unless question

    answers.where(game_question_id: question.id).count
  end

  def option_answer_counts(question = current_question)
    return {} unless question

    answers.where(game_question_id: question.id).group(:game_option_id).count
  end

  def moderator_state_key
    "m-#{status}-q#{current_question_index}-v#{version}"
  end

  def player_state_key(player, answer = nil)
    if player.nil?
      "u-#{finished? ? "finished" : "join"}"
    else
      "p-#{status}-q#{current_question_index}-v#{version}-a#{answer&.game_option_id}"
    end
  end

  def start!
    with_lock do
      return false unless lobby?

      if game_questions.empty?
        update!(
          status: "finished",
          started_at: Time.current,
          finished_at: Time.current,
          version: version + 1
        )
      else
        update!(
          status: "question_open",
          current_question_index: 0,
          started_at: Time.current,
          version: version + 1
        )
      end
      true
    end
  end

  def finish_question!
    with_lock do
      return false unless question_open?

      update!(
        status: "question_closed",
        version: version + 1
      )
      true
    end
  end

  def next_question!
    with_lock do
      return false unless question_closed?

      next_idx = current_question_index + 1
      if next_idx < game_questions.count
        update!(
          status: "question_open",
          current_question_index: next_idx,
          version: version + 1
        )
      else
        update!(
          status: "finished",
          finished_at: Time.current,
          version: version + 1
        )
      end
      true
    end
  end

  def end_game!
    with_lock do
      return false if finished?

      update!(
        status: "finished",
        finished_at: Time.current,
        version: version + 1
      )
      true
    end
  end

  def join_player!(name)
    trimmed = name.to_s.strip
    return nil if trimmed.blank?

    with_lock do
      return :finished if finished?

      player = players.create!(name: trimmed)
      update!(version: version + 1)
      player
    end
  end

  def record_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)
    return :closed if player.nil?

    with_lock do

      return :invalid unless option

      answer = answers.find_or_initialize_by(player: player, game_question: question)
      if answer.game_option_id != option.id
        answer.game_option = option
        answer.save!
        update!(version: version + 1)
      end
      answer
    end
  end
end

    assert_not_equal game.id, game2.id

    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    alice = game.join_player!("  Alice  ")
    assert_equal "Alice", alice.name
    assert_equal 1, game.players_count

    assert game.start!
    assert game.question_open?
    q1 = game.current_question
    wrong_opt = q1.game_options.find_by!(correct: false)
    right_opt = q1.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)

    assert_kind_of Answer, game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: wrong_opt.id)
    assert_equal wrong_opt.id, alice.answer_for(q1).game_option_id

    # Changing answer updates the same Answer record
    assert_kind_of Answer, game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: right_opt.id)
    assert_equal 1, game.answers.count
    assert_equal right_opt.id, alice.answer_for(q1).game_option_id

    assert game.finish_question!
    assert game.question_closed?
    assert_equal :closed, game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: wrong_opt.id)
    assert_equal right_opt.id, alice.answer_for(q1).game_option_id

    assert_not game.last_question?
    assert game.next_question!
    assert game.question_open?
    assert_equal 1, game.current_question_index
    assert game.last_question?

    assert game.finish_question!
    assert game.end_game!
    assert game.finished?

    assert_equal :finished, game.join_player!("Late Bob")
    assert_equal 1, game.players_count
  end

  test "quiz with zero active questions finishes immediately on start" do
    @q1.update!(active: false)
    @q3.update!(active: false)

    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    assert_equal 0, game.total_questions
    assert game.start!
    assert game.finished?
  end
end

    assert game.last_question?

    assert game.finish_question!
    assert game.end_game!
    assert game.finished?

    assert_equal 1, game.players_count

class QuizImportExportTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "export_payload writes exact keys in order with both active and correct" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Frontend Fest 2026")
    q1 = create_question(quiz, "First?", active: true, options: [ [ "A1", false ], [ "A2", true ] ])
    q2 = create_question(quiz, "Second?", active: false, options: [ [ "B1", true ], [ "B2", true ], [ "B3", false ] ])
    q2.move_up!

    payload = quiz.reload.export_payload
    assert_equal [ :title, :questions ], payload.keys
    assert_equal "Frontend Fest 2026", payload[:title]
    assert_equal 2, payload[:questions].size

    exported_q1, exported_q2 = payload[:questions]
    assert_equal [ :text, :active, :options ], exported_q1.keys
    assert_equal "Second?", exported_q1[:text]
    assert_equal false, exported_q1[:active]
    assert_equal [
      { text: "B1", correct: true },
      { text: "B2", correct: true },
      { text: "B3", correct: false }
    ], exported_q1[:options]
    exported_q1[:options].each { |opt| assert_equal [ :text, :correct ], opt.keys }

    assert_equal [ :text, :active, :options ], exported_q2.keys
    assert_equal "First?", exported_q2[:text]
    assert_equal true, exported_q2[:active]
    assert_equal [
      { text: "A1", correct: false },
      { text: "A2", correct: true }
    ], exported_q2[:options]
  end

  test "import creates a new quiz with defaults and preserves order even with duplicate title" do
    existing = Quiz.create!(title: "Frontend Fest 2026")

    json = <<~JSON
      {
        "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
        "questions": [
          {
            "text": "Q1?",
            "options": [
              {"text": "Wrong"},
              {"text": "Right", "correct": true}
            ]
          },
          {
            "text": "Q2?",
            "active": false,
            "options": [
              {"text": "Alpha", "correct": true},
              {"text": "Beta", "correct": false},
              {"text": "Gamma", "correct": true}
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    JSON

    importer = QuizImport.new(json)
    assert importer.save, importer.errors.inspect

    imported = importer.quiz
    assert_not_equal existing.id, imported.id
    assert_equal 2, Quiz.where(title: "Frontend Fest 2026").count

    questions = imported.questions.order(:position, :id).to_a
    assert_equal [ "Q1?", "Q2?" ], questions.map(&:body)
    assert_equal [ true, false ], questions.map(&:active)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2 ], questions.map(&:position)

    assert_equal [ "Wrong", "Right" ], questions[0].options.pluck(:body)
    assert_equal [ false, true ], questions[0].options.pluck(:correct)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2 ], questions[0].options.pluck(:position)

    assert_equal [ "Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma" ], questions[1].options.pluck(:body)
    assert_equal [ true, false, true ], questions[1].options.pluck(:correct)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3 ], questions[1].options.pluck(:position)
  end

  test "import allows zero questions" do
    importer = QuizImport.new({ title: "Empty Quiz", questions: [] }.to_json)
    assert importer.save
    assert_equal "Empty Quiz", importer.quiz.title
    assert_equal 0, importer.quiz.questions.count
  end

  test "import rejects invalid JSON and rule violations atomically without partial writes" do
    invalid_payloads = [
      "",
      "   ",
      "{not valid json",
      "[]",
      '"just a string"',
      { questions: [] }.to_json,
      { title: "   ", questions: [] }.to_json,
      { title: 123, questions: [] }.to_json,
      { title: "No questions key" }.to_json,
      { title: "Bad questions", questions: "oops" }.to_json,
      { title: "Blank question", questions: [ { text: "  ", options: [ { text: "A", correct: true }, { text: "B" } ] } ] }.to_json,
      { title: "Bad active", questions: [ { text: "Q?", active: "yes", options: [ { text: "A", correct: true }, { text: "B" } ] } ] }.to_json,
      { title: "One option", questions: [ { text: "Q?", options: [ { text: "A", correct: true } ] } ] }.to_json,
      { title: "No correct", questions: [ { text: "Q?", options: [ { text: "A" }, { text: "B", correct: false } ] } ] }.to_json,
      { title: "Blank option", questions: [ { text: "Q?", options: [ { text: "A", correct: true }, { text: "  ", correct: false } ] } ] }.to_json,
      { title: "Bad correct", questions: [ { text: "Q?", options: [ { text: "A", correct: "yes" }, { text: "B", correct: true } ] } ] }.to_json,
      # Second question invalid after a valid first question -> nothing created!
      {
        title: "Partial failure",
        questions: [
          { text: "Valid Q1", options: [ { text: "A", correct: true }, { text: "B" } ] },
          { text: "Invalid Q2", options: [ { text: "Only one", correct: true } ] }
        ]
      }.to_json
    ]

    invalid_payloads.each do |payload|
      assert_no_difference [ "Quiz.count", "Question.count", "Option.count" ] do
        importer = QuizImport.new(payload)
        assert_not importer.save, "Expected payload to fail: #{payload}"
        assert_not_empty importer.errors
        assert_nil importer.quiz
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def create_question(quiz, body, active:, options:)
    q = quiz.questions.build(body: body, active: active)
    rows = {}
    options.each_with_index do |(text, correct), idx|
      rows[idx.to_s] = { "body" => text, "correct" => correct ? "1" : "0" }
    end
    q.assign_option_rows(rows)
    q.save_with_options!
    q
  end

    assert_equal "First?", exported_q2[:text]
    assert_equal true, exported_q2[:active]
    assert_equal [

      { text: "A2", correct: true }
    ], exported_q2[:options]
  end

    assert_not_equal existing.id, imported.id
    assert_equal 2, Quiz.where(title: "Frontend Fest 2026").count

      { title: "   ", questions: [] }.to_json,
      { title: 123, questions: [] }.to_json,
      { title: "No questions key" }.to_json,
      { title: "Bad questions", questions: "oops" }.to_json,
      { title: "Blank question", questions: [ { text: "  ", options: [ { text: "A", correct: true }, { text: "B" } ] } ] }.to_json,

      { title: "One option", questions: [ { text: "Q?", options: [ { text: "A", correct: true } ] } ] }.to_json,
      { title: "No correct", questions: [ { text: "Q?", options: [ { text: "A" }, { text: "B", correct: false } ] } ] }.to_json,
      { title: "Blank option", questions: [ { text: "Q?", options: [ { text: "A", correct: true }, { text: "  ", correct: false } ] } ] }.to_json,
      { title: "Bad correct", questions: [ { text: "Q?", options: [ { text: "A", correct: "yes" }, { text: "B", correct: true } ] } ] }.to_json,

        title: "Partial failure",

          { text: "Invalid Q2", options: [ { text: "Only one", correct: true } ] }
        ]
      }.to_json

        assert_not_empty importer.errors
        assert_nil importer.quiz
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def create_question(quiz, body, active:, options:)
    q = quiz.questions.build(body: body, active: active)
    rows = {}
    options.each_with_index do |(text, correct), idx|
      rows[idx.to_s] = { "body" => text, "correct" => correct ? "1" : "0" }
    end
    q.assign_option_rows(rows)
    q.save_with_options!
    q
  end

**Deep Dive into Real-Time Game Broadcasting**

Okay, let's get laser-focused on this latency issue. We need to ensure every player, across big screens and phones, gets the questions *instantly* and in sync with the moderator. I'm going to meticulously review `app/models/game_broadcaster.rb` and `app/javascript/controllers/live_game_controller.js`, hunting for any subtle snags.

First, I'm starting with `GameBroadcaster.broadcast_players_stage(game)`.  Why did they use `game.players.find_each`? For a large game, that looks like it could become a bottleneck. We are doing one query to select 1000 players at a time, and then iterating on each player with a new `Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to` call. I need to understand what `Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to` does behind the scenes.  Ah, it generates a stream name (which encodes the Game and Player IDs) and then uses `ActionCable.server.broadcast`. With the async adapter, that's almost instantaneous per player. Still, if we're dealing with hundreds of players, that's potentially inefficient, especially during status transitions.

For cases like "question_closed" and "finished", it's doing per-player rendering which looks expensive, since each player has a `player_answer` that must be displayed. If it's "finished", we should precompute that leaderboard only once, and pass it into the `render_html` method for each player.  Let's make sure `Game#leaderboard` is highly optimized to load the required data (players, game questions, answers including game options) with minimal queries (ideally 2 or 3 fast ones!).  Then we compute the leaderboard once and pass it as a local into the render for the player. Perfect!

Now, let's switch gears and go into `app/views/play/show.html.erb` and `app/views/moderate/games/show.html.erb` and `live_game_controller.js` to see what is going on. We need to make sure we're handling all WebSocket connection or drop scenarios and that the JavaScript is rock solid. I need to trace `live_game_controller.js` line by line, really understanding how the connection state is managed.

Okay, here's what `live_game_controller.js` is doing: It observes the `connected` attribute on `this.streamSource` and on initial load, it either calls `this.sync()` or if it's not immediately connected, it sets a timeout and retries `this.startPolling()`.  Let's consider what happens when Turbo Streams replaces the content? In the player side, `<div id="player_stage">` is the content replaced. So `turbo-cable-stream-source` and `#player_root` are kept, which means that the Stimulus controller's stateTarget will automatically update and the controller will continue observing. On the moderator's side, the same occurs with `<span id="moderator_state_marker">` which is replaced. So the controller's targets are updated. So far, so good.

Now, what happens on the `PlayController#join` method? The user goes to `/play/:code` and submits the form to join the game. `form_with` uses Turbo by default, so on submit, Turbo Drive kicks in and replaces the entire body with the new `play/show.html.erb`. This means the `live_game_controller#connect()` will rerun, observe the `<turbo-cable-stream-source>`, and when it's `connected`, call `this.sync()`. That makes total sense!

But wait, how does `<turbo-cable-stream-source>` actually connect?  I need to go deeper into `turbo.js` to confirm its behavior. I'm going to grep `connected` in `turbo-rails`'s `turbo.js` to verify. I need to be 100% certain that `<turbo-cable-stream-source>` does what we expect and sets the `connected` attribute consistently.

class Quiz < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :active_questions, -> { where(active: true).order(:position, :id) }, class_name: "Question"
  has_many :games, dependent: :destroy

  before_validation :normalize_title

  validates :title, presence: true
  validates :winners_count, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 1 }

  def export_payload
    {
      title: title,
      questions: questions.includes(:options).order(:position, :id).map do |question|
        {
          text: question.body,
          active: question.active?,
          options: question.options.sort_by { |opt| [ opt.position, opt.id ] }.map do |option|
            {
              text: option.body,
              correct: option.correct?
            }
          end
        }
      end
    }
  end

  private

  def normalize_title
    self.title = title.to_s.strip

class Game < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed finished].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K L M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  LeaderboardEntry = Data.define(:player, :place, :points, :total_time, :winner) do
    def player_id
      player.id
    end

    def name
      player.name
    end

    def winner?
      winner
    end
  end

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :quiz_title, presence: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :winners_count, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 1 }

  def self.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    transaction do
      game = create!(
        quiz: quiz,
        quiz_title: quiz.title,
        winners_count: quiz.winners_count,
        code: generate_unique_code,
        status: "lobby",
        current_question_index: 0,
        version: 1
      )

      quiz.active_questions.includes(:options).order(:position, :id).each_with_index do |question, q_idx|
        gq = game.game_questions.create!(
          body: question.body,
          position: q_idx + 1
        )

        question.options.sort_by { |o| [ o.position, o.id ] }.each_with_index do |option, o_idx|
          gq.game_options.create!(
            body: option.body,
            correct: option.correct?,
            position: o_idx + 1
          )
        end
      end

      game
    end
  end

  def self.generate_unique_code
    loop do
      code = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET.sample }.join
      return code unless exists?(code: code)
    end
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question_open?
    status == "question_open"
  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"
  end

  def finished?
    status == "finished"
  end

  def ordered_questions
    game_questions.includes(:game_options).order(:position, :id).to_a
  end

  def total_questions
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_question
    return nil if lobby? || finished?

    ordered_questions[current_question_index]
  end

  def last_question?
    total = total_questions
    total.zero? || current_question_index >= total - 1
  end

  def players_count
    players.count
  end

  def current_answers_count
    question = current_question
    return 0 unless question

    answers.where(game_question_id: question.id).count
  end

  def option_answer_counts(question = current_question)
    return {} unless question

    answers.where(game_question_id: question.id).group(:game_option_id).count
  end

  def moderator_state_key
    "m-#{status}-q#{current_question_index}-v#{version}"
  end

  def player_state_key(player, answer = nil)
    if player.nil?
      "u-#{finished? ? "finished" : "join"}"
    else
      "p-#{status}-q#{current_question_index}-v#{version}-a#{answer&.game_option_id}-w#{player.winner? ? 1 : 0}"
    end
  end

  def start!
    with_lock do
      return false unless lobby?

      now = Time.current
      questions = ordered_questions
      if questions.empty?
        update!(
          status: "finished",
          started_at: now,
          finished_at: now,
          version: version + 1
        )
      else
        questions.first.update!(opened_at: now)
        update!(
          status: "question_open",
          current_question_index: 0,
          started_at: now,
          version: version + 1
        )
      end
      true
    end
  end

  def finish_question!
    with_lock do
      return false unless question_open?

      update!(
        status: "question_closed",
        version: version + 1
      )
      true
    end
  end

  def next_question!
    with_lock do
      return false unless question_closed?

      next_idx = current_question_index + 1
      questions = ordered_questions
      if next_idx < questions.size
        questions[next_idx].update!(opened_at: Time.current)
        update!(
          status: "question_open",
          current_question_index: next_idx,
          version: version + 1
        )
      else
        update!(
          status: "finished",
          finished_at: Time.current,
          version: version + 1
        )
      end
      true
    end
  end

  def end_game!
    with_lock do
      return false if finished?

      update!(
        status: "finished",
        finished_at: Time.current,
        version: version + 1
      )
      true
    end
  end

  def join_player!(name)
    trimmed = name.to_s.strip
    return nil if trimmed.blank?

    with_lock do
      return :finished if finished?

      player = players.create!(name: trimmed)
      update!(version: version + 1)
      player
    end
  end

  def record_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)
    return :closed if player.nil?

    with_lock do
      return :closed unless question_open?

      question = current_question
      return :closed unless question && question.id == game_question_id.to_i

      option = question.game_options.find_by(id: game_option_id)
      return :invalid unless option

      answer = answers.find_or_initialize_by(player: player, game_question: question)
      if answer.new_record? || answer.game_option_id != option.id
        answer.game_option = option
        answer.answered_at = Time.current
        answer.save!
        update!(version: version + 1)
      end
      answer
    end
  end

  def leaderboard
    questions_by_id = game_questions.index_by(&:id)
    all_players = players.order(:created_at, :id).to_a
    correct_answers_by_player = answers
      .includes(:game_option)
      .select { |answer| answer.game_option.correct? }
      .group_by(&:player_id)

    scored = all_players.map do |player|
      player_answers = correct_answers_by_player[player.id] || []
      points = player_answers.size
      total_time = player_answers.sum do |answer|
        question = questions_by_id[answer.game_question_id]
        opened = question&.opened_at || started_at || question&.created_at || answer.created_at
        picked = answer.answered_at || answer.updated_at || opened
        [ picked - opened, 0.0 ].max
      end

      {
        player: player,
        points: points,
        total_time: total_time
      }
    end

    sorted = scored.sort_by do |row|
      [ -row[:points], row[:total_time], row[:player].created_at, row[:player].id ]
    end

    sorted.each_with_index.map do |row, idx|
      LeaderboardEntry.new(
        player: row[:player],
        place: idx + 1,
        points: row[:points],
        total_time: row[:total_time],
        winner: row[:player].winner?
      )
    end
  end

  def pick_top_winners!
    with_lock do
      return false unless finished?

      winner_ids = leaderboard
        .select { |entry| entry.points.positive? }
        .first(winners_count)
        .map(&:player_id)

      apply_winners!(winner_ids)
      true
    end
  end

  def draw_winners!
    with_lock do
      return false unless finished?

      eligible = leaderboard.select { |entry| entry.points.positive? }
      winner_ids = if eligible.size <= winners_count
        eligible.map(&:player_id)
      else
        nth_points = eligible[winners_count - 1].points
        guaranteed = eligible.select { |entry| entry.points > nth_points }
        remaining = winners_count - guaranteed.size
        tied_pool = eligible.select { |entry| entry.points == nth_points }

        (guaranteed + tied_pool.sample(remaining)).map(&:player_id)
      end

      apply_winners!(winner_ids)
      true
    end
  end

  def reset_winners!
    with_lock do
      return false unless finished?

      apply_winners!([])
      true
    end
  end

  private

  def apply_winners!(winner_ids)
    transaction do
      players.update_all(winner: false)
      players.where(id: winner_ids).update_all(winner: true) if winner_ids.any?
      players.reset
      update!(version: version + 1)
    end
  end
end
EOF

class GameBroadcaster
  class << self
    def broadcast_moderator_stage(game, join_url: nil)
      game = game.reload
      leaderboard = game.finished? ? game.leaderboard : nil
      stage_html = render_html("moderate/games/stage", game: game, join_url: join_url, leaderboard: leaderboard)
      marker_html = render_html("moderate/games/state_marker", game: game)

      stream = turbo_stream_replace("big_screen_stage", stage_html) +
               turbo_stream_replace("moderator_state_marker", marker_html)

      Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, :moderator ], content: stream)
    end

    def broadcast_moderator_counters(game)
      game = game.reload
      marker_html = render_html("moderate/games/state_marker", game: game)

      if game.lobby?
        counter_html = render_html("moderate/games/lobby_players_count", game: game)
        stream = turbo_stream_replace("lobby_players_count", counter_html) +
                 turbo_stream_replace("moderator_state_marker", marker_html)
        Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, :moderator ], content: stream)
      elsif game.question_open? || game.question_closed?
        counter_html = render_html("moderate/games/question_answers_counter", game: game)
        stream = turbo_stream_replace("question_answers_counter", counter_html) +
                 turbo_stream_replace("moderator_state_marker", marker_html)
        Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, :moderator ], content: stream)
      end
    end

    def broadcast_players_stage(game)
      game = game.reload

      case game.status
      when "question_open"
        stage_html = render_html("play/stage", game: game, player: true, player_answer: nil)
        stream = turbo_stream_replace("player_stage", stage_html)
        game.players.find_each do |player|
          Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, player ], content: stream)
        end
      when "question_closed"
        current_q = game.current_question
        answers_by_player_id = if current_q
          game.answers.where(game_question_id: current_q.id).includes(:game_option).index_by(&:player_id)
        else
          {}
        end

        game.players.find_each do |player|
          stage_html = render_html(
            "play/stage",
            game: game,
            player: player,
            player_answer: answers_by_player_id[player.id]
          )
          stream = turbo_stream_replace("player_stage", stage_html)
          Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, player ], content: stream)
        end
      when "finished"
        entries = game.leaderboard
        entries_by_player_id = entries.index_by(&:player_id)
        total_players = entries.size

        game.players.find_each do |player|
          stage_html = render_html(
            "play/stage",
            game: game,
            player: player,
            player_answer: nil,
            leaderboard: entries,
            leaderboard_entry: entries_by_player_id[player.id],
            total_players: total_players
          )
          stream = turbo_stream_replace("player_stage", stage_html)
          Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, player ], content: stream)
        end

        join_stage_html = render_html("play/stage", game: game, player: nil, player_answer: nil)
        join_stream = turbo_stream_replace("player_stage", join_stage_html)
        Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, :join ], content: join_stream)
      end
    end

    private

    def render_html(partial, locals)
      ApplicationController.renderer.render(
        partial: partial,
        formats: [ :html ],
        locals: locals
      )
    end

    def turbo_stream_replace(target, html)
      %(<turbo-stream action="replace" target="#{target}"><template>#{html}</template></turbo-stream>\n)
    end
  end
end
EOF

messages.thinking:
**Comprehensive Testing Strategy for New Features**

Okay, so the existing tests all pass – excellent! But now, it's time to shift gears and think *deeply* about edge cases and ensure we've got bulletproof tests for every single new feature. Let's start with a systematic review of each requirement:

1.  **Quiz Settings:** The "Number of winners" setting is straightforward, with validation and persistence. However, the critical question is what happens when this setting is *changed* after a quiz is created. We need tests to confirm that new games get the updated value, while older games retain the value they had at creation. We'll also verify the UI updates correctly based on the number of winners.

2.  **Scoring and Speed Ranking:** This is where things get interesting. We've got the point system nailed down, and the rules around speed are well-defined. But, that corner case where a user clicks an option, waits, and clicks a different one, and then circles back to the original option... We need to handle *that*. The existing logic, `if answer.new_record? || answer.game_option_id != option.id`, appears to be correct. We'll add a test to verify that the `answered_at` is only updated when a new option is *actually* selected, not for repeated taps on the same option.

    We need to also test that the points are not shown during gameplay, so let's verify that the views don't show any scores.

3.  **Instantaneous Live Updates:** ActionCable Turbo Streams should handle the updates smoothly. We need to verify that we are indeed broadcasting everything quickly and efficiently. We also need to check the broadcasting order (`broadcast_moderator_stage` before `broadcast_players_stage`) and ensure that rendering is optimized for the expected number of players, even if the user re-clicks an answer. We also need to test `bin/serve` in production mode to verify that the app boots correctly and that WebSockets work correctly.

4.  **Leaderboard and Phone Results:** We need to cover the leaderboard display and the information on player phones after the quiz ends. We need to handle the scenarios where a user joins mid-game and is still accurately ranked.

5.  **Picking the Winners - Rules and Edge Cases:** This area requires careful testing of several distinct scenarios. We need tests to cover edge cases with `"Top N"` for a variety of numbers of players, including those with zero points. The `"Draw"` feature presents randomness, and we need tests to handle the different cases, so we'll test that the ties are broken as expected. We'll ensure that the `"Reset winners"` function works as expected and that the live updates work. Furthermore, we must also test the moderator authentication, ensuring that only authenticated users can trigger these actions.

To make sure everything is covered, we're going to create the following tests:

*   Unit tests in `test/models/quiz_test.rb` and/or `test/models/game_test.rb` to cover model-level validations and logic related to quiz settings, scoring, speed ranking, and winner selection.

require "test_helper"

class GameTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActiveSupport::Testing::TimeHelpers

  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "RubyConf Quiz")
    @q1 = @quiz.questions.create!(body: "What is 2+2?", active: true)
    @q1.assign_option_rows({
      "0" => { "body" => "3", "correct" => "0" },
      "1" => { "body" => "4", "correct" => "1" }
    })
    @q1.save_with_options!

    @q2 = @quiz.questions.create!(body: "Inactive question", active: false)
    @q2.assign_option_rows({
      "0" => { "body" => "A", "correct" => "1" },
      "1" => { "body" => "B", "correct" => "0" }
    })
    @q2.save_with_options!

    @q3 = @quiz.questions.create!(body: "Capital of France?", active: true)
    @q3.assign_option_rows({
      "0" => { "body" => "Paris", "correct" => "1" },
      "1" => { "body" => "Lyon", "correct" => "0" }
    })
    @q3.save_with_options!
  end

  test "quiz winners_count defaults to 3 and requires integer >= 1" do
    assert_equal 3, @quiz.winners_count

    [ 0, -1, 1.5, nil, "" ].each do |invalid|
      @quiz.winners_count = invalid
      assert_not @quiz.valid?, "Expected winners_count=#{invalid.inspect} to be invalid"
    end

    @quiz.winners_count = 5
    assert @quiz.valid?
  end

  test "create_from_quiz! snapshots only active questions, winners_count, and generates unique code" do
    @quiz.update!(winners_count: 2)
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)

    assert_equal "RubyConf Quiz", game.quiz_title
    assert_equal 2, game.winners_count
    assert_equal "lobby", game.status
    assert_match(/\A[A-Z2-9]{5}\z/, game.code)
    assert_equal [ "What is 2+2?", "Capital of France?" ], game.game_questions.pluck(:body)

    # Later edits to quiz do not change existing game
    @quiz.update!(winners_count: 5, title: "Changed")
    assert_equal 2, game.reload.winners_count
    assert_equal "RubyConf Quiz", game.quiz_title

    game2 = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    assert_not_equal game.code, game2.code
    assert_not_equal game.id, game2.id
    assert_equal 5, game2.winners_count
  end

  test "full game lifecycle, last answer wins, and rejects late answers" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    alice = game.join_player!("  Alice  ")
    assert_equal "Alice", alice.name
    assert_equal 1, game.players_count

    assert game.start!
    assert game.question_open?
    q1 = game.current_question
    assert_not_nil q1.opened_at
    wrong_opt = q1.game_options.find_by!(correct: false)
    right_opt = q1.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)

    assert_kind_of Answer, game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: wrong_opt.id)
    assert_equal wrong_opt.id, alice.answer_for(q1).game_option_id

    # Changing answer updates the same Answer record
    assert_kind_of Answer, game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: right_opt.id)
    assert_equal 1, game.answers.count
    assert_equal right_opt.id, alice.answer_for(q1).game_option_id

    assert game.finish_question!
    assert game.question_closed?
    assert_equal :closed, game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: wrong_opt.id)
    assert_equal right_opt.id, alice.answer_for(q1).game_option_id

    assert_not game.last_question?
    assert game.next_question!
    assert game.question_open?
    assert_equal 1, game.current_question_index
    assert game.last_question?

    assert game.finish_question!
    assert game.end_game!
    assert game.finished?

    assert_equal :finished, game.join_player!("Late Bob")
    assert_equal 1, game.players_count
  end

  test "quiz with zero active questions finishes immediately on start" do
    @q1.update!(active: false)
    @q3.update!(active: false)

    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    assert_equal 0, game.total_questions
    assert game.start!
    assert game.finished?
  end

  test "leaderboard ranks by points then speed of correct answers using last pick" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    alice = game.join_player!("Alice")
    bob = game.join_player!("Bob")
    charlie = game.join_player!("Charlie")
    dave = game.join_player!("Dave")

    travel_to Time.zone.local(2026, 11, 23, 12, 0, 0) do
      assert game.start!
      q1 = game.current_question
      q1_right = q1.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)
      q1_wrong = q1.game_options.find_by!(correct: false)

      # Alice picks right at 1s, switches to wrong at 2s, switches back to right at 6s -> 6s for Q1
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_wrong.id)
      # Bob picks right at 3s -> 3s for Q1
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
      # Charlie picks wrong at 1s -> 0 pts, 0s counted
      game.record_answer!(player: charlie, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_wrong.id)
      travel 3.seconds
      game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)

      assert game.finish_question!
      assert game.next_question!

      q2 = game.current_question
      q2_right = q2.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)
      q2_wrong = q2.game_options.find_by!(correct: false)

      # Q2 opens at t=6s.
      # Charlie picks right at +1s -> total: 1 pt, 1s
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: charlie, game_question_id: q2.id, game_option_id: q2_right.id)
      # Alice picks wrong at +1s -> total: 1 pt, 6s (wrong Q2 time not counted)
      game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q2.id, game_option_id: q2_wrong.id)
      # Bob picks right at +2s -> total: 2 pts, 5s
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: q2.id, game_option_id: q2_right.id)
      # Dave never answers -> 0 pts

      assert game.finish_question!
      assert game.end_game!
    end

    board = game.leaderboard
    assert_equal [ "Bob", "Charlie", "Alice", "Dave" ], board.map(&:name)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ], board.map(&:place)
    assert_equal [ 2, 1, 1, 0 ], board.map(&:points)
    assert_in_delta 5.0, board[0].total_time, 0.01
    assert_in_delta 1.0, board[1].total_time, 0.01
    assert_in_delta 6.0, board[2].total_time, 0.01
    assert_in_delta 0.0, board[3].total_time, 0.01
  end

  test "picking top N, drawing ties, ignoring zero-point players, and resetting winners" do
    @quiz.update!(winners_count: 2)
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    p1 = game.join_player!("P1") # 2 pts
    p2 = game.join_player!("P2") # 1 pt (fast)
    p3 = game.join_player!("P3") # 1 pt (medium)
    p4 = game.join_player!("P4") # 1 pt (slow)
    p5 = game.join_player!("P5") # 0 pts

    # Cannot pick winners before game finishes
    assert_not game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_not game.draw_winners!
    assert_not game.reset_winners!

    travel_to Time.zone.local(2026, 11, 23, 12, 0, 0) do
      game.start!
      q1 = game.current_question
      q1_right = q1.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)
      q1_wrong = q1.game_options.find_by!(correct: false)

      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: p1, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
      game.record_answer!(player: p2, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: p3, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: p4, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_right.id)
      game.record_answer!(player: p5, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: q1_wrong.id)

      game.finish_question!
      game.next_question!

      q2 = game.current_question
      q2_right = q2.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)
      travel 1.second
      game.record_answer!(player: p1, game_question_id: q2.id, game_option_id: q2_right.id)
      game.finish_question!
      game.end_game!
    end

    # Top 2 -> P1 and P2
    assert game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_equal [ p1.id, p2.id ], game.leaderboard.select(&:winner?).map(&:player_id)

    # Reset -> no winners
    assert game.reset_winners!
    assert_empty game.leaderboard.select(&:winner?)

    # Draw -> P1 always wins (2 pts > 1 pt), remaining 1 spot drawn randomly among P2/P3/P4
    seen_drawn = Set.new
    30.times do
      assert game.draw_winners!
      winners = game.leaderboard.select(&:winner?).map(&:player_id)
      assert_equal 2, winners.size
      assert_includes winners, p1.id
      refute_includes winners, p5.id
      drawn = (winners - [ p1.id ]).first
      assert_includes [ p2.id, p3.id, p4.id ], drawn
      seen_drawn << drawn
    end
    assert_equal 3, seen_drawn.size, "Expected Draw to pick uniformly without speed bias"

    # If winners_count > players with points, only players with points win (0-point never win)
    game.update!(winners_count: 10)
    assert game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_equal [ p1.id, p2.id, p3.id, p4.id ], game.leaderboard.select(&:winner?).map(&:player_id)
    assert_not p5.reload.winner?

    assert game.draw_winners!
    assert_equal [ p1.id, p2.id, p3.id, p4.id ], game.leaderboard.select(&:winner?).map(&:player_id)
    assert_not p5.reload.winner?
  end

  test "zero players with points produces zero winners" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    p1 = game.join_player!("Zero1")
    p2 = game.join_player!("Zero2")
    game.start!
    game.end_game!

    assert game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_empty game.players.where(winner: true)
    assert game.draw_winners!
    assert_empty game.players.where(winner: true)
  end
end

require "application_system_test_case"

class PrizesAndLeaderboardTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Prizes Live Quiz")

    @q1 = @quiz.questions.create!(body: "Fastest language?", active: true)
    @q1.assign_option_rows({
      "0" => { "body" => "C", "correct" => "1" },
      "1" => { "body" => "Turtle", "correct" => "0" }
    })
    @q1.save_with_options!

    @q2 = @quiz.questions.create!(body: "Web framework?", active: true)
    @q2.assign_option_rows({
      "0" => { "body" => "Rails", "correct" => "1" },
      "1" => { "body" => "Pencil", "correct" => "0" }
    })
    @q2.save_with_options!
  end

  test "quiz settings validation, scoring by speed, leaderboard, and live winner picking" do

    # Reset winners removes winners live everywhere

    [ :bob, :alice, :charlie, :dave ].each do |session|

    leaders = all("ol.leaderboard > li")
    within(leaders[0]) { assert_text "Winner" }
    within(leaders[3]) { assert_no_text "Winner" }
    assert_equal 1, [ leaders[1], leaders[2] ].count { |li| li.text.include?("Winner") }

    Capybara.using_session(:bob) { assert_text "You won!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:dave) { assert_no_text "You won!" }
  end
end

messages.content: I will add `html: { novalidate: true }` to `app/views/moderate/quizzes/_form.html.erb` so server-side validation renders the `.errors` box consistently while keeping `min="1"` on the number input, then re-run the full test suite.
messages.thinking:
**Analyzing Form Validation Behavior**

Okay, here's the situation. I was looking at `quizzes/_form.html.erb` and realized something about the interaction between the HTML5 `min` attribute and form submission. If we have `min: 1` on a number field *without* `novalidate`, the browser throws its own native tooltip when the user enters `0`. This is annoying. However, if QA tries to fill in `0` and checks if it's not saved, or checks for `.errors`, this needs to work consistently.

The question then is, how do we make validation consistent while still keeping the `min: 1` attribute for the spinner? What if we add `novalidate: true` to the `form_with` call?

Let's think. If we keep the input field `min: 1` and also use `html: { novalidate: true }` in `form_with`, we still get `type="number"`, `min="1"`, and `step="1"` on the `<input>`. Crucially, if someone enters `0` (or clears the field), the form *submits* to Rails, fails validation (returning a `422`), and re-renders the form with the `.errors` box. The record *does not save*! This means we get the Rails validation error message, not the native browser tooltip.

I noticed that in `questions/_form.html.erb` and `quizzes/_form.html.erb`, neither `title` nor `body` are marked as `required: true`. Instead, all the validation is done using the `.errors` pink box, as per the `styleguide.html`. Therefore, using `html: { novalidate: true }` on `quizzes/_form.html.erb` keeps `min="1"`, makes the "Number of winners" validation consistent with "Title" and "Question", and ensures the error is clearly displayed.

So, the plan is to update `app/views/moderate/quizzes/_form.html.erb` with `html: { novalidate: true }` and then re-run the system tests to confirm the change behaves correctly.

arguments.command:
sed -i 's/form_with model: \[ :moderate, @quiz \] do |f|/form_with model: [ :moderate, @quiz ], html: { novalidate: true } do |f|/' /app/app/views/moderate/quizzes/_form.html.erb
cd /app && bin/rails test && bin/rails test:system

Okay, here's what I'm thinking:

**Release Testing and Documentation Rollout!**

Alright, that's a *massive* sigh of relief! The unit, integration, and system tests all passed. The 23 unit/integration tests with their 559 assertions and the 6 system tests with 244 assertions – *perfect*. We're looking solid on that front.

Now, though, we need to really put it through its paces in a *production-like* environment. Time to test `bin/serve` with `RAILS_ENV=production`. Let's grab a free port and hit it with a `GET /up` to ensure it's healthy. Important to check that asset compilation goes off without a hitch. And, of course, a real production request – the whole shebang – and we'll ensure clean cleanup afterwards. Gotta cover all the bases!

Also, I have to update `docs/architecture.md`. Gotta capture Release 3's key features: the scoring, the timing mechanisms, how the leaderboard works, and how the winner is selected. We'll add those notes.

Finally, assuming it's configured, I should run `rubocop` to make sure we're clean on code style before wrapping things up.

cd /app
PORT=3099 RAILS_ENV=production SECRET_KEY_BASE=testsecretkeybase1234567890abcdef QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=admin QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=secret bin/serve > /tmp/quizzy_prod.log 2>&1 &
PID=$!
trap "kill $PID 2>/dev/null || true" EXIT

for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:3099/up | grep -q 200; then

  fi

done

kill $PID 2>/dev/null || true
wait $PID 2>/dev/null || true

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' >> /app/docs/architecture.md

## Prizes, Scoring & Leaderboard (Release 3)
- **Quiz Settings (`quizzes.winners_count`)**:
  - Integer `>= 1`, defaults to `3`, labeled `"Number of winners"` in quiz settings (`Moderate::QuizzesController`, `Quiz`).
  - Snapshotted onto `games.winners_count` when `Game.create_from_quiz!` creates a game.
- **Timing & Scoring**:
  - `game_questions.opened_at` records the exact timestamp when a question opens (`Game#start!`, `Game#next_question!`).
  - `answers.answered_at` records the timestamp of the player's last pick (`Game#record_answer!`).
  - Each correct answer scores 1 point; ties in points are broken by lower total response time across correct answers only (`answered_at - opened_at`). Points are never shown on players' phones while the game is in progress.
- **Leaderboard & Winner Selection (`Game#leaderboard`, `players.winner`)**:
  - After `"End quiz"`, the big screen displays `<ol class="leaderboard">` with place, name, points (`"2 points"`, `"1 point"`, `"0 points"`), and `"Winner"` badges; each player's phone displays `"Place X of Y"`, points, and `"You won!"` if selected as a winner.
  - Moderator controls (`Moderate::GamesController#top_winners`, `#draw_winners`, `#reset_winners`) update `players.winner`, increment `game.version`, and broadcast live to `[game, :moderator]` and each `[game, player]`:
    - `"Top N"` picks the first `N` players with `> 0` points.
    - `"Draw"` guarantees every player with strictly more points than N-th place and draws remaining spots at random among all players tied at N-th place's points (ignoring speed).
    - Players with `0` points never win; if fewer than `N` players have points, all of them win.
    - `"Reset winners"` clears all winners.
EOF

cd /app
rm -f storage/production.sqlite3*
bin/rubocop --format simple 2>/dev/null || true
bin/rails test && bin/rails test:system
